AltMed Investigation

By: Mart-Marie Faure | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Desperate to find a cure for his cancer and save his leg, young Kyle Nhlapo, turns to expensive alternative treatments. Funds are raised but in the end it all went horribly wrong..

Unique Selling Point:
Desperate to find a cure for his cancer 20 year old Kyle Nhlapo hoped that an alternative cancer treatment called RIGVIR would save his leg and cure his Osteocarcoma. Kyle was referred to the Charlotte Maxeke hospital in 2018 where he was admitted and diagnosed with Osteosarcome. He started chemo therapy in March 2018. He became extremely ill from the treatment and his mother Beulah started looking for alternatives. They found a treatment called RIGVIR administered by a clinic called ALTMED. The treatment came at a huge cost and Kyle and Beulah contacted Hot FM (HotCares) to assist them in raising the funds. HotCares and a private donor raised almost R500 000 for the treatment.
First Kyle was told that a body cleansing had to be done. He was put on a Vitamin C IV drip costing R32 168.00. After a month's cleansing they were told that RIGVIr was the best option. The clinic explained that the treatment was very costly and hoped that they had the funds. The clinic recommended treatment for three months. They gave a breakdown of the cost of the treatment. R180 000 for the first month. After receiving 4 injections there was no sign of the promised cure and no shrinkage of the tumour.. Beulah then wrote to Latvia where RIGVIR is developed asking about the treatment. She was told that they had no data of treating Osteosarcoma. Beulah and Kyle approached Altmed and informed them that they were terminating the treatment. By then , Kyle needed an amputation. Kyle and Beulah then requested a refund of the donated money. This was declined. Altmed did refund enough for the amputation but the balance of almost R80 000.00 was not refunded claiming that it was administration costs.


Summary:
RIGVIR is a Latvia-invented injectable cancer drug. It is a virotherapy medication approved in 2004, by the State Agency of Medicines of the Republic of Latvia. However in march 2019 the distribution in Latvia was stopped by the State Agency of Medicines after laboratory tests found that the amount of ECHO-7 virus was in much smaller amounts than claimed. The licence was suspended and RIGVIR removed from sale.
Oncologist Dr David Gorski wrote " There are many mysterious aspects to the RIGVIR story that strongly suggests that RIGVIR is cancer quackery.
The Latvian State Agency of Medicines sent a sample to a laboratory in the UK. the found it to have very little ECHO-7 virus. ZVA's laboratory director described it " its like expecting lemon juice and getting lemon flavoured water." RIGVIR is no stranger to controversy, with questions asked repeatedly about the validity of its clinical claims, methods of marketing itself to cancer patients across the world.

Press Release:


Miracle Cure or Cancer Quackery?
Moved by the plight of a 19-year old man with a rare cancerous tumour on his leg, radio listeners crowdfund for an expensive alternative treatment. The injectable drug is administered and marketed through a private Johannesburg clinic that makes bold promises that it is his last hope of achieving remission or extension of life. But the young man’s condition shows no improvement, and it seems they can’t save his leg. In agony, he struggles to access the remainder of the donations to pay for his prosthesis. Carte Blanche tracks down the origins of the purported miracle treatment to Latvia, where it has since been banned - and asks how the money was spent.
Producer: Mart-Marie Faure
Presenter: Devi Sankaree-Govender

Promo 1: 11”

A young man is diagnosed with a life threatening bone cancer. Funds are raised to pay for a controversial alternate treatment. But in the end things go terribly wrong.

Promo 3: 11” –

Diagnosed with a rare life threatening bone cancer, a desperate young man turns to a Jhb alternative medicines clinic for answers but it’s expensive and the treatment isn’t legal in south africa.

KYLE NHLAPO
A rare bone cancer changed the life of nineteen year old Kyle Nhlapo in an instant. In February last year he was diagnosed with Osteosarcoma, an aggressive and life-threatening bone cancer. He urgently needed treatment...


But the treatment came at a cost, way out of the family’s reach. Johannesburg radio station Hot 91.9FM heard Kyle’s plea and stepped in.



And on behalf of Hot FM and Monte we donate R125 000.



Oh my goodness, I am so grateful It means as much to me this journey has been such a struggle. I want to thank you from the bottom of my heart.

A total of R525 000 was raised. The money was to be used for an expensive alternative treatment because.
Kyle found chemotherapy DEBILITATING.

Beulah

Kyle’s mother

The chemo didn’t work so well for Kyle. He was very sick…. Couldn’t eat



Kyle and his mother Beulah Andrews searched the internet for alternatives treatments.




They found a treatment called Rigvir, developed in Latvia, in eastern Europe. It CONSISTS OF onco-lit-tic viruses, which are injected into the body. THE VIRUSES find cancer cells, penetrates them, multiplies and destroys the cancer.

STRAP:
Kyle Nhlapo




Some cancer sufferers choose to explore alternative treatments, with positive results.


Basically we had searched that treatment and found that Altmed Care was offering that type of treatment in SA. So I wanted to try something different and I wanted to save my leg. We had placed a lot of hope in this treatment…they said this treatment had a proven track record and has helped a lot of people with their cancers.




Devi V/O **The AltmedCare Clinic and the LXM Humanitarian Foundation were Co-founded by Drs Steven Gunn and Brett Phillips -- to help patients with terminal diseases such as cancer and HIV and to facilitate and manage donor funds. THE CLINIC OFFERS holistic and alternative treatments such as RIGVIR.
Devi V/O









But Rigvir is highly controversial.

Our research revealed that as far back as 2017 the Latvian Oncologists Association had asked for the product to be withdrawn as clinical data supporting its efficay was of poor quality.

An expose by the Latvian investigative television program, De Facto, revealed that the Rigvir which is supposed to fight cancer, contained far less of the actual active virusES than it promised, and had little effect.

UNDERCOVER


Strap
Hidden Camera

Graphic:

Treatment Costs:
Month 1: R180 000
Month 2: R145 000
Month 3: R145 000
Total: R470 000 WE went UNDERCOVER TO ESTABLISH HOW Altmed JUSTIFIES the use of Rigvir. We were seen by doctors Steven Gunn and Brett Phillips, both AltMed practitioners and co-directors of the company.
______________________________________________

What options are available?

Most of those treatments to be honest actually we actually do. From the nutritional treatment, dietary intervention right through to Rigvir viral therapy from Latvia. In every single case where we have treated the patient with the virus and our other therapy they have lived longer than predicted. We physically fly over there every year and bring a massive batch with us to SA. It’s for all cancers except the blood cancers. ______________________________________________

THESE WERE SIMILAR ASSURRANCES GIVEN TO KYLE AND HIS MOM.

With THE DONOR MONEY in pocket, Kyle signed up for the FULL three-month course at a cost of R470 000 rand.

After the first part of the treatment, consisting of 4 prime booster injections, costing R180,000, Kyle STOPPED HIS TREATMENT.

KYLE
Up sound After the first month, that’s when we stopped, because we could see it wasn’t working. It hadn’t changed anything in terms of my situation. I mean my tumour was still the same size, so we just knew it wasn’t the right treatment.

Kyle And what did he say?

He said that we should continue until three months and see what happens afterward. 00:15:53The clinic had suggested the amputation before we started the treatment because they cannot guarantee remission.

Carmen, Hot FM
We were guaranteed that they would have R278,000 available for Kyle to continue his treatment through amputation and surgery and recovery process.
Devi V/O
***Kyle’’S LEG WAS AMPUTATED AT A COST OF just over a R119 000 Rands – (paid for) WITH the left over MONEY. THE MONEY WAS BEING MANAGED BY DR GUNN’S LXM Humanitarian Foundation.

Devi Question

Carmen

Devi Question


Carmen


Devi Question

Carmen
So in your mind, how much is still owed to Kyle?

00:11:17: About R84 000.


Where is the money?

00;11:22 : They deducted and administration fee of about R78 000. They offered to pay the R5 000 that was remaining .


00:13: 43. What is wrong with this?.

There is a young man at stake and his future. And when money was donated by good people, for a specific reason, that is what it should be used for.
Devi V/O IN A JOINT INTERVIEW, Altmed Care Clinic’s Dr Steven Gunn and the director for the LXM Humanitarian foundation Trisch Rose-emer EXPLAINED WHAT HAPPENED to THE leftover DONOR MONEY, INTENDED for Kyle’s prosthesis. INSTEAD, IT WAS ALLOCATED as an administration fee.
Trisch


Devi

Trisch


Devi




STRAP
Trisch Rosema
Director: LXM Humanitarian Foundation

Devi



Trisch

Let’s just knock out the issue of the admin fee now. Why was this not disclosed in writing?

Admittedly it was my fault, each letter is written individually, and in the haste, my haste to assist Kyle I didn’t write it. I had already sent the letter off to him but I did speak to him about it personally and to his mom, Beulah

You say you did, they say you didn’t. So all I can go on is the letter. This is a serious missed of you to not include it in the letter.

It is. Is it a 15% admin fee? Well its a fee, no its not really an administration fee, we use the term loosely. The fee actually goes back in the foundation, to assist other people who cant raise funds or haven’t raised enough funds.

00:01:58 What is the right thing to do?

We are allowed to take a 15% administration fee, we will talk to the board and make a decision. We know what is the right thing to do. We already said we will waiver it.
Devi V/O








DEVI
STRAP:
Dr Kaizer Thembo
Head: Complementary Medicines SAHPRA Money WASN’T THE ONLY issue. THE treatment offered by Dr Gunn is illegal and hadn’t been registered with the South African Health Products Regulatory Council -- Dr Kai-zer Thembo HEADS UP COMPLEMENTARY MEDICINES at SAPHRA.



So do all medicines need to be registered in order for them to be used legally in South Africa?

The act prescribes for purposes of sale all medicines shall be registered.
Devi V/O Gunn was unapologetic about prescribing an unregistered medicine...
Devi



Dr Gunn

Devi


Dr Gunn
You say you had to do something with a therapy that is not registered for use in South Africa.


No it's not true, its not registered in South Africa,

What does that mean Dr Gunn if something is not registered in South Africa.

It means, Medicines Control Council or SAHPRA does not have it on their list as a registered medication or drug.
Dr Gunn

STRAP
Dr Steven Gunn
Co-Founder:
AltmedCare Cliic











Devi





Dr Gunn




Devi





Devi V/O








Devi




Gunn








Devi V/O



Trisch
















Devi V/O





















However the law allow s for emergency situations via section 21 of the health act.

Well I sent the application and before even I could get any reply he had already stopped the treatment.



“We got in touch with the Latvian State Agency of Medicines, they had it tested in the UK. Their director said and I quote you think that you get lemon juice but in fact it is lemon flavoured water.”


Well first of all, all it was- was actually less viral numbers than what was stated originally and from a scientific point of view anyway, if you have less number than what is stated it does not mean it will not work.

You are disagreeing...with the Latvian State Agency Medicines?


I am saying that you stating what's implied that its watered down. In other words it is not very effective. For thats not a scientific statement
______________________________________________
**IN AN EMAIL TO US, SAPHPRA CONFIRMD THERE WAS A SHORT PERIOD IN 2018 WHEN DR GUNN APPLIED, FOR VARIOUS PATIENTS, TO USE THE UNREGITERED RIGVIR, HOWEVER KYLE NHLAPO was NOT ONE OF THEM.
They go on to SAY THAT DR GUNN MUST SUBSTANTIATE WHY HE IS MARKETING THE UNREGISTERD PRODUCT AS CATAGORY D.
IN ADDITION, THE MARKETING AND PROMOTION OF UREGISTERED MEDICINES IS PROHIBITED IN `SOUTH AFRICA.
FURTHER TO THIS, THE LATVIAN REGULATORY BODY HAS WITHDRAWN THE REGISTRATION CERTIFICATE FOR RIGVIR DUE TO ITS LACK OF EFFICACY. NO FURTHER SECTION 21 APPLICATIONS FOR RIGIVR WILL BE APPROVED.

______________________________________________
Section 21 is a section within the medicines act which allows for the request of importation of medicine for personal use and it is mainly in cases where certain medical conditions are not met and can be applied for from time to time but it needs to be motivated for.
______________________________________________

Do you understand that whatever your reasoning is that you were actually not allowed to administer that particular treatment to Kyle?

Yes but a very good reason why I did that.

Will that reason stand up in court.

I was in a timeline element that was to decide between waiting for weeks or months for MCC to reply or to.

Try and save my patients life. And I took the option on my conscious and as a good doctor to try and save the patient's life.
You could not guarantee that this treatment was going to work for an osteosarcoma.

Correct you cannot guarantee if chemotherapy is going to work either.
But one therapy is legal and the other is not legally used in SA as far as Kyle is concerned.
Correct but this was a unique situation.



Then when we questioned Roserma about funding and the use of an illegal product, things heated up.


----------------------------------------------------------------------------
Does the patient not take any responsibility for using a medication that isn't approved?

Maybe look to yourselves first.

Listen, I can stand up and look at myself in the mirror, because I have treated hundreds of thousands of patients. I have put myself out there to save people’s lives.


Gunn insists that using Rigvir, an, unregistered treatment in South Africa, is still the right thing to do.

After the traumatic amputation of his leg that Kyle so desperately, wanted to avoid. Scans have shown that he is now in remission.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Desperate to find a cure for his cancer and save his leg, young Kyle Nhlapo, turns to expensive alternative treatments. Funds are raised but in the end it all went horribly wrong..
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Desperate to find a cure for his cancer 20 year old Kyle Nhlapo hoped that an alternative cancer treatment called RIGVIR would save his leg and cure his Osteocarcoma. Kyle was referred to the Charlotte Maxeke hospital in 2018 where he was admitted and diagnosed with Osteosarcome. He started chemo therapy in March 2018. He became extremely ill from the treatment and his mother Beulah started looking for alternatives. They found a treatment called RIGVIR administered by a clinic called ALTMED. The treatment came at a huge cost and Kyle and Beulah contacted Hot FM (HotCares) to assist them in raising the funds. HotCares and a private donor raised almost R500 000 for the treatment. First Kyle was told that a body cleansing had to be done. He was put on a Vitamin C IV drip costing R32 168.00. After a month's cleansing they were told that RIGVIr was the best option. The clinic explained that the treatment was very costly and hoped that they had the funds. The clinic recommended treatment for three months. They gave a breakdown of the cost of the treatment. R180 000 for the first month. After receiving 4 injections there was no sign of the promised cure and no shrinkage of the tumour.. Beulah then wrote to Latvia where RIGVIR is developed asking about the treatment. She was told that they had no data of treating Osteosarcoma. Beulah and Kyle approached Altmed and informed them that they were terminating the treatment. By then , Kyle needed an amputation. Kyle and Beulah then requested a refund of the donated money. This was declined. Altmed did refund enough for the amputation but the balance of almost R80 000.00 was not refunded claiming that it was administration costs.
metadata.Summary: RIGVIR is a Latvia-invented injectable cancer drug. It is a virotherapy medication approved in 2004, by the State Agency of Medicines of the Republic of Latvia. However in march 2019 the distribution in Latvia was stopped by the State Agency of Medicines after laboratory tests found that the amount of ECHO-7 virus was in much smaller amounts than claimed. The licence was suspended and RIGVIR removed from sale. Oncologist Dr David Gorski wrote " There are many mysterious aspects to the RIGVIR story that strongly suggests that RIGVIR is cancer quackery. The Latvian State Agency of Medicines sent a sample to a laboratory in the UK. the found it to have very little ECHO-7 virus. ZVA's laboratory director described it " its like expecting lemon juice and getting lemon flavoured water." RIGVIR is no stranger to controversy, with questions asked repeatedly about the validity of its clinical claims, methods of marketing itself to cancer patients across the world.
